record.original_question: What are the singularities of the nested Hilbert scheme Hilb_{d1,d2}(A^2) parameterizing flags Γ1 ⊆ Γ2 of degrees d1 and d2? In particular, can this scheme be nonreduced?

evidence.quote: Problem X. What are the singularities of Hilbd1,d2(A^2)? Can it be nonreduced?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{A}^2$ denote the affine plane over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $d_1 \le d_2$ be positive integers. The nested Hilbert scheme $\mathrm{Hilb}_{d_1,d_2}(\mathbb{A}^2)$ is the scheme parameterizing pairs $(\Gamma_1, \Gamma_2)$ of zero-dimensional closed subschemes of $\mathbb{A}^2$ with $\Gamma_1 \subseteq \Gamma_2$, $\deg \Gamma_1 = d_1$, and $\deg \Gamma_2 = d_2$. 

Describe the singularities of $\mathrm{Hilb}_{d_1,d_2}(\mathbb{A}^2)$. In particular, determine whether $\mathrm{Hilb}_{d_1,d_2}(\mathbb{A}^2)$ can be nonreduced for some pair $(d_1, d_2)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is the subject of active research with partial results. The nested Hilbert scheme $\mathrm{Hilb}^{n,2}(S)$ on a smooth surface is known to have rational singularities, and more recently the cases $\mathrm{Hilb}^{n,3}$ and $\mathrm{Hilb}^{n,4}$ have been shown to have canonical Gorenstein singularities. Irreducibility and singularity-type results have been established for further families, but a complete classification of singularities of $\mathrm{Hilb}_{d_1,d_2}(\mathbb{A}^2)$ for general $(d_1,d_2)$ — and the question of whether it can be nonreduced — does not appear to be settled in the literature.

status_evidence.snippet: Hilb^{n,2}(S) has rational singularities for any smooth surface S.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result on singularities of nested Hilbert schemes.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies irreducibility and singularities of certain Hilb^{n_1,n_2}(S).
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on singularity questions for nested Hilbert schemes.

status_evidence.title: Singularities of the nested Hilbert scheme of points of length 3,4
status_evidence.snippet: Hilb^{n,3} and Hilb^{n,4} have canonical Gorenstein singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress on singularity types.
